headline: Beat the first frost this week—harvest tomatoes, peppers, squash and basil before a killing frost lands.

tasks.title: Rescue warm-season crops
tasks.detail: Zone 6a's first killing frost usually arrives mid-October, so pick all tomatoes (ripe and blush), peppers, summer/winter squash, beans and basil now. Ripen green tomatoes indoors on a counter or in a paper bag.

tasks.title: Plant garlic
tasks.detail: Mid-to-late October is prime for zone 6a. Break a head into cloves and plant pointy-end up, 2–3 inches deep and 6 inches apart in a sunny bed, then top with a few inches of straw mulch.

tasks.title: Leave the frost-sweeteners
tasks.detail: Don't rush kale, Brussels sprouts, carrots, parsnips and leeks—a light frost makes them noticeably sweeter. Keep harvesting as you need them; they'll hold in the ground for weeks.

tasks.title: Plant spring bulbs
tasks.detail: Now through early November is the window for daffodils, tulips, crocus and alliums. Plant roughly three times as deep as the bulb is tall, pointy-end up, in well-drained soil for color next spring.

tasks.title: Clear spent plants
tasks.detail: Pull finished annual veggies and pull or cut back anything with mildew, blight or spots. Trash or bin diseased foliage—don't compost it—to keep fungal problems from overwintering in your beds.

tasks.title: Put empty beds to bed
tasks.detail: Mulch cleared beds with shredded leaves or straw, or sow a quick cover crop like winter rye if time allows. Keep a floating row cover handy to shield any tender crops if a frost night threatens before you've harvested.
